newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 11.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* La Spezia magistrates say public works minister and former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro is not under preliminary investigation for alleged corruption after his name has been mentioned in wiretappings (all).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro asks the government to cut his privileges as "great sacrifices are imposed on citizens with the 1997 budget" (all)

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said the 1997 budget goes in the right direction but warned it might not be enough to meet EMU criteria. Fazio also cautioned that the austerity budget could slow down economic growth (all).
* State telecom holding Stet is joining French building company Bouygues and Germany's Veba to set up a rival telecommunication system to France Telecom (all).
* Italian new car registrations fell 8.55 percent to 116,000 units in September (all).
* Speaking to the Industry commission in Senate, Olivetti chief executive Roberto Colaninno said the group has found a buyer for its ailing PC division (all).
* The Treasury is due to unveil today the decree which will set out the privatisation of troubled Banco di Napoli (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
